{{Short description|List of host nations of the FLLA World Cup}}

The '''[[FLLA World Cup]]''' is an international [[Arraby]] competition contested by the senior men's national teams of the member associations of the [[FLLA]]. Since the inaugural tournament in 1656, staged at the time as the Ayuman Continental Tournament, the competition has been hosted by a single country or, on three occasions, jointly by a group of co-hosting countries. This article lists every host nation of the tournament, together with the continent on which each edition was held and a summary of hosting by nation and by confederation.

Twenty-four editions have been completed between 1656 and the [[1764 FLLA World Cup|1764 edition]]. A further four scheduled editions, in [[1664 FLLA World Cup|1664]], [[1688 FLLA World Cup|1688]], [[1692 FLLA World Cup|1692]] and [[1696 FLLA World Cup|1696]], were awarded but never contested because of intercontinental conflict. The right to host the tournament has, since the FLLA Council adopted a formal confederation rotation policy in February 1740, passed between the seven continental confederations in a fixed sequence; before that date hosts were selected under an informal framework that tended to alternate between [[Ayuma|Ayuman]] and non-Ayuman countries.<ref name="fllarotation">{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/governance/host-rotation-policy|title=The confederation host-rotation policy|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=17 February 1764}}</ref>

All six [[Ayuma|Ayuman]] member associations to have hosted the tournament did so before the rotation policy took full effect; the most recent six editions, from the [[1744 FLLA World Cup|1744 edition]] onwards, have each been staged on a different continent in rotation.<ref name="fllaheritage">{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/heritage/world-cup/roll-of-honour|title=FLLA World Cup roll of honour|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=20 August 1764}}</ref>

[[Emara]] is the most frequent host of the FLLA World Cup, having staged the tournament three times. Five further nations, [[Easuhura]], [[Praesyu]], [[Lycroa]], [[Raledria]] and [[United Delet]], have hosted twice each; [[Raledria]] is the only one of these to have done so on a continent other than [[Ayuma]].<ref name="fllaheritage" />

The [[AYFVL]] (Ayuman) confederation has hosted fourteen of the twenty-four completed editions, more than the other six confederations combined. Every Ayuman hosting predates the universal application of the confederation rotation policy; under that policy, in force since the [[1744 FLLA World Cup|1744 edition]], the tournament has rotated through [[Ayuma]], [[Atirha]], [[New Ayre]], [[Quia]] and back to [[Ayuma]], with the [[Mahea|Mahean]], [[Massir]]i and [[Acrola]]n confederations each having hosted once.<ref name="fllarotation" />

With the [[1768 FLLA World Cup|1768]], [[1772 FLLA World Cup|1772]] and [[1776 FLLA World Cup|1776]] editions awarded to [[Sanagara]] ([[Massir]]), [[Pelugrotoa]] ([[Mahea]]) and the [[Ahokini]]–[[Ashain]] co-host group ([[Quia]]) respectively, every one of the seven confederations will have hosted the tournament at least twice by the close of the 1776 cycle.

==Cancelled editions==

Four editions of the competition were awarded a host but never contested. The [[1664 FLLA World Cup|1664 edition]], allocated to [[Alzurian Union|Alzuria]], was cancelled following the outbreak of the [[Great Imperial War]]. The [[1688 FLLA World Cup|1688]], [[1692 FLLA World Cup|1692]] and [[1696 FLLA World Cup|1696]] editions were cancelled because of the [[Red War]] (1688 to 1695) and the subsequent reconstruction; the 1688 edition had been awarded to [[Raledria]] and had reached the stage of stadium allocation before hostilities forced its abandonment.<ref name="fllaredwar">{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/heritage/history/red-war-cancellations|title=The Red War and the cancelled editions of 1688, 1692 and 1696|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=30 May 1763}}</ref> The hosts of these cancelled editions are not counted in the hosting totals above.

==Future hosts==

Three forthcoming editions have confirmed hosts, each selected under the confederation rotation policy:

* The [[1768 FLLA World Cup|1768 edition]] will be held in [[Sanagara]], returning the tournament to [[Massir]] for the first time since [[1732 FLLA World Cup|1732]]. Sanagara was awarded the edition at the FLLA Council meeting of 28 September 1764.<ref name="flla1768award">{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/news/1764/sanagara-awarded-1768|title=Sanagara awarded the 1768 FLLA World Cup|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=28 September 1764}}</ref>
* The [[1772 FLLA World Cup|1772 edition]] will be held in [[Pelugrotoa]], the second edition to be staged in [[Mahea]].
* The [[1776 FLLA World Cup|1776 edition]] will be co-hosted by [[Ahokini]] and [[Ashain]], the second edition to be held in [[Quia]] and the second to use co-hosts.
